title: Classify mixed Q8 call-space shear identities; no pair of shear images separates (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped proof with an exact finite certificate, plus a conjecture. No new κ.** The package is `research/q8-mixed-shear-identity-space`.

The question comes from unpaidmoon's #4378, which leaves open whether shape (4,1) (four `[zi]` targets, one `[zj]`) needs 13 or 15 positive i/j calls in the `F2[Q8]` dirty-register model. The homogeneous 3t proof (PR3558) uses the identities `X K Y = 0` and `X K^2 Y = 0`. This PR determines what the mixed model offers in place of that pair.

- **Theorem A (finite certificate plus written proof).** Take active compressions `X M_w Y` of the 30 label-block monomials `E L E … L E` with at most three factors `L`, together with `P_i` and `P_j`. The linear identities valid for every exact word, of any shape and any finite dirty workspace, are exactly the 7-dimensional span of the `F2[Q8]` coefficient equations. Twenty-five explicit exact words give compression rows of rank 25 out of 32.
- **Theorem B.** Exactly four shears `I+h` with `deg h ≤ 2` satisfy `X(I+h)Y = 0`: PR3570's `K1` and `K2`, and two cubic shears `Q1` and `Q2`. None of the 12 shear products of degree at most three is an identity.
- **Theorem C.** Every one of the six pairs of images `K1U, K2U, Q1U, Q2U` (with `U = im Y`) meets on an exact one-role three-call word. A two-image cyclic-style argument therefore cannot certify `n ≥ 3t` for mixed words in this calculus.
- **Conjecture D (unproved).** `dim(K1U+K2U+Q1U+Q2U) ≥ 2t` for every exact word. This would imply `n ≥ 3t` for every mixed shape, hence 15 at (4,1) and 24 at (7,1). It holds on every exact mixed-label word in complete meet-in-the-middle censuses: one role at length 3, and two roles at lengths 5–8. Together these cover 62,444 mixed-label words through length 7 and 407,296 at length 8. All censused shapes have `t ≤ 2`, where 3t is already known.

The (4,1) minimum is **not** decided.

## Reproduce

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/q8-mixed-shear-identity-space
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/q8-mixed-shear-identity-space --check-source-history
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/q8-mixed-shear-identity-space/verify.py          # ~15 s, registered
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/q8-mixed-shear-identity-space/verify.py --full   # ~3 min, opt-in length-8 census
```

All four commands passed locally (CPython 3.12, standard library only). The registered check took about 20 s through the package runner. The verifier writes no files.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- Theorem A covers degree ≤ 3 only. It excludes neither higher-degree compression identities, nor rank arguments that are not linear identities, nor arguments using dirty rows and columns.
- Conjecture D has finite evidence only.
- No physical caller, routing, restoration, hosting, precision or supplier is priced.
- Not run: Lean, Docker and the selected cold replay.
- Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Prove Conjecture D. A proof closes both open lengths of #4378. First test three-role length-9 words with t = 3.
2. Which compression identities exist at degree four and higher? Two-role length-8 samples leave a 16-dimensional annihilator at degree five, possibly small-dimension artefacts.
3. Is there a 13-call (4,1) word? It would refute D. A search restricted to PR3536 six-role cores would be the first step.

## Related open work

- #6038 (conjugate-pair target, four calls in every group): a different target and model, with no shared quantity.
- #3906 (Q8 dirty spectator restoration audit): an audit of the restoration boundary. It computes no compression identities.
- #6037 (balanced depth-three chain multiplicities): a different object (connector chains), with no shared quantity.

## Credit

Builds on PR3517, PR3536, PR3558 and PR3570 (Nick Petalas), cited and not re-audited. The open question is from unpaidmoon's #4378.
